client_brief:
Coffee sticker collection: recover four designs, add two, prepare the cutting sheet

Four recovered designs + two new designs = one six-sticker collection for Meridian & Ash.

We are looking for a designer who can move comfortably from artwork recovery into original drawing. The window and bag photographs establish the first four designs; the two new pieces should belong naturally beside them.

Please think about the physical sticker from the start. The collection needs intentional negative space, clean offset cuts and a gang sheet that makes sense for the printer.

Design collection
Six sticker designs as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: four recovered from photographs of painted and printed originals and two authored to match their construction. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Cutting paths
Six single closed offset paths at the offset the printer's note states, each held as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork, with interior negative space resolved deliberately and any contour simplified for the blade named as simplified. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Production sheet
One sheet at the printer's true sheet size in real physical units, all six designs ganged with the stated minimum gutter and safe margin honoured, the arrangement chosen between a tight pack and themed rows and justified on vinyl yield and counter readability, with the cut layer present and separable on the sheet.

We are open to a tight pack or themed rows. Choose the stronger arrangement and explain the trade-off between sheet yield and how the collection reads; do not leave two unfinished directions for us to resolve.

Supplied references and printer information: meridian_window_mark.jpg (4160 x 3120); meridian_shelfcard_2025.pdf; meridian_sheet_spec.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: meridian_bag_illustrations/ (3 frames, 5472 x 3648); meridian_origins.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Please work within $1,200-$3,200 fixed and the 7 to 15 business days target. Allow for one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-04 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. The shape recurs constantly on Upwork and Freelancer.com under titles of the form 'die cut sticker sheet design for our coffee brand' and 'convert my logo to vector for stickers', and the body is always the same three asks: turn our existing logo and artwork into vector, arrange the designs on one print ready sheet, and supply the cut lines, with 'vector files' and 'editable source files' named among the deliverables and the client volunteering that all they have is a photograph or a printed sample because the original designer is gone. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted verbatim into the client voice here: pull our logo and a few of our existing printed illustrations into clean sticker art, and lay it all out as a die-cut sheet plus individual stickers we can sell and hand out. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and the reason it needed strengthening is that as carved it sat almost entirely on one surface (trace, then lay out), which is not the commission a roastery of this size actually places. Two things change that. First, the ledger's own 'peel-mockup card' would be photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as the printed counter card the roastery already puts in front of each origin, and that card is a genuine record per page run off a press PDF they already own. Second, CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes authored fixed canvas layout at true sheet size real, with inline SVG arriving as native editable vector, so the sheet and the on sale set are one editable document rather than a flat picture. That is the fuller job this client genuinely places inside one month.

price_band_and_audience: Impulse retail at three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack, buyer twenty to thirty five, a cafe regular who buys at the till without deciding first. The band is load-bearing. At this price the range has to read as abundant and hand made: many small pieces, a warm printed ground, generous ink coverage, type that looks painted rather than set. The same six marks treated as a luxury programme, one foil emblem on a deep matte ground with acres of air, misreads the till entirely: it prices like a forty dollar object, it kills the four pack, and it makes the giveaway handful look like a mistake. Push the other way into loud discount styling, heavy outlines, drop shadows and a crowded sheet, and it stops reading as a roastery that people want to advertise on a laptop lid. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Specialty coffee roaster and cafe selling stickers and merchandise at the till, at farmers markets and to wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon, a converted machine shop with one counter, two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.about: Meridian and Ash roast single origin coffee in a converted machine shop and sell it across their own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. The merchandise table is half the fun: stickers people put on laptops and water bottles because they actually like the mark. The whole point is a range that feels made by hand, not bought by the case.
brand_identity.audience: Cafe regulars twenty to thirty five who buy a sticker at the till without deciding first, and wholesale buyers who hand them out with orders.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Impulse retail, three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack. Priced to be handed out by the fistful, so the range has to read as abundant rather than precious.
brand_identity.typography: A shaded serif wordmark that looks painted rather than set, arched over a filled roundel. Text and labels lean into a friendly, slightly irregular hand. Nothing boutique or foil thin.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, a little wry, never precious. Example line: Pull one off the sheet, stick it on your laptop, come back for the other three.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No usable source files exist. The window mark was hand painted on the shop glass in 2018 by a sign painter who never handed over a file. The three current illustrations survive only printed on the coffee bags, and the printer still holds last season's counter card artwork.
brand_identity.values: Consistency people can trust, so the artwork stops being redrawn slightly differently every batch, and a hand made feel that reads as a real roastery rather than a franchise.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_window_mark.jpg (4160 x 3120)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the shop window from the sidewalk, the mark hand painted in two inks on the glass: a shaded serif wordmark arched over a filled roundel that carries an ash leaf inside a hairline ring.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark exists. Ross painted it in 2018 and we never got a file off him."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup painted on glass, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the window or the glass returns the pane rather than the paint, a compound prompt returns the arched wordmark while silently dropping the ring and the leaf and still looks entirely plausible, and the one call knockout cannot punch the ring's enclosed interior so it returns a solid opaque disc. Across the right third the street reflects in the glass at close to the value of the darker ink.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_bag_illustrations/ (3 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Flat lay photographs of three printed coffee bags, one illustration on each: a moth, a ridge line, a pour over cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The three that are already on the bags. We want those exactly as they are, they are the reason people pick us up."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the three were printed as solid ink and the third was screened at press. At photograph preview scale a screen reads as a flat tone and is indistinguishable from solid ink, so nothing about the frame declares which is which. It only announces itself once the ink is traced, as thousands of dot contours instead of a drawing. Separately one of the three crosses the bag's gusset fold, so part of its geometry is bent off the plane and does not straighten with the frame.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_shelfcard_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press artwork for last season's counter card, one card per origin, the file that actually went to press.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer sends this back every season. The holders on the counter are cut for it, so the card cannot change size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's origin name, roast line, tasting notes and price were set as one continuous flow, so what the converted document exposes as separately addressable frames is nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows. And the readout of the card's own story omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length, while the mapping validates clean and the prepare call reports success.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_origins.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data for the six current origins: origin, farm, process, roast, tasting notes, price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six we are pouring now. The notes are what our head roaster wrote, do not improve them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six carry a second tasting line the other four do not, so those two rows are roughly twice the length of their neighbours, and one row's price is the wholesale per pound figure rather than the counter price, which no column header distinguishes and no cell flags.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_sheet_spec.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The sticker printer's note: sheet size, minimum gutter between cuts, safe margin from the sheet edge, and their standing requirement that the cut contour arrive as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer sent when we asked what they need."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the three bag illustrations was screened at press rather than printed in solid ink. At the scale a photograph of a bag previews at, a press screen reads as a flat tone and is visually identical to solid ink, so nothing in the frame, the filename or the client's description separates them. It declares itself only in the traced result: the two solid marks come back as a drawing with a countable number of contours, and the screened one comes back as thousands of dot contours that still assemble into a plausible looking picture at full canvas and only fall apart as artwork at sticker size and as an editable object once placed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no options at all and the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, which is the decision this checkpoint is about. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the three illustrations are already printed on the bags and that the client wants them exactly as they are. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected illustration goes through a different chain, a binary ink mask traced as a mask rather than a colour plate traced as art, or a redraw as authored geometry when the screen has destroyed the line.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive that one illustration through a different route, judge whether what comes back is still the drawing on the bag or a new drawing wearing its shape, and then re-place it, which changes its silhouette and therefore its cut contour and its position in the sheet arrangement.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A range where one of six stickers is a cloud of dots that prints muddy at fifty five millimetres and arrives in the client's editable file as thousands of loose shapes, on a merchandise line whose entire premise is that nobody ever has to redraw the artwork again.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the readout of the shelf card's own text is short of the truth. The card's copy was set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows, and the readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed. Every offset computed past the omission is short by that run's length. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those offsets, the prepare call reports completing successfully, and the only place the shortfall appears is on the merged page, where two fields still carry last season's copy while the rest carry this season's.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the readout is the only description of the story the tools volunteer, and there is no flag, warning or count that says a run is missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer still has last season's artwork and that the cards must stay the same size. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to reconstruct the card's true story text out of the interchange file and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different derivation, not the same derivation repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the field map from the reconstructed story text, prepare the template again, confirm by round tripping the interchange file that every placeholder is actually present rather than trusting the success message, then re-merge and read the six pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six counter cards that look right and print right and quietly tell every customer at the till the wrong tasting notes and the wrong price for two of the six origins, with every tool response in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the whole deliverable turns on. The printer needs the cut contour as a separable object sitting over the artwork, and the natural authoring constructions for it are exactly the ones this importer discards without saying so: an outline is dropped entirely, a stroked display letterform loses its stroke and can render as fully transparent, a blurred halo is dropped so the element goes hard edged, and a stacked shadow is truncated to its first layer. All of them return success. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so whichever canvas is not first cannot be checked any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only that the cut line arrive as its own thing the printer can lift off. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different construction of the same object, a closed path drawn as real geometry with its own fill and stroke rather than a CSS effect around the artwork, and the sheet then has to be re-composed around what that object actually is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the cut layer as authored path geometry, re-author the sheet and the on sale canvases around it, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gang sheet delivered as an editable file with no cut layer in it at all on the canvases nobody looked at, sent to the printer who then does exactly what the last supplier's press operator did and redraws the cut by hand, which is the specific thing the client hired this job to stop.

decision_gates: Selection wording on the painted window: naming the window or the glass takes the pane, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a one call knockout on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which recovery route each of the four originals needs, since a two colour trace off a binary mask and a colour accurate knockout plate produce different artwork and the response text is identical.
Whether a recovered illustration is still the drawing on the bag or has become a new drawing wearing its shape, and what to tell the client when it is the second.
How the two new designs are constructed, taken from the recovered marks' own stroke weight and terminals rather than chosen freely.
Cut contour craft: offset direction, what happens to enclosed interior negative space, and when to simplify a contour the blade cannot follow.
Tight pack versus themed rows on the sheet, argued on vinyl yield against readability in a counter bin.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a three dollar impulse buy, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the licensed kraft frame joins the range's world or reads as bought, and how warm the ground can go before the ink stops separating from it.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of coffee stickers. IDENTITY: this is the mark a sign painter put on this roastery's window in 2018 and three illustrations that are already printed on bags customers recognise on the shelf, and the entire reason the job exists is that a supplier keeps redrawing them slightly differently. A regenerated mark is precisely the failure the client is paying to stop. SPEC: the printer needs six closed cut contours at a stated offset as separable objects on a sheet at a real physical size with a stated gutter, and the counter cards must land at last season's exact trim so the existing holders still fit, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the sheet and the on sale set are defined by being editable, because the six designs rotate and the owners cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: is this illustration solid ink or a press screen, does this cut layer still exist after the import, did two of the six cards quietly keep last season's copy.
